rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - no criminal-record inquiry before conditional offer
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not use an application containing criminal-record questions, or make any oral or written criminal-record inquiry, before making a conditional offer to rent. Exceptions cover methamphetamine manufacture or production on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers offering rental dwelling units for residential purposes, other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are not covered. A provider may consider whether an applicant was convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime sex offender registration requirement.
rules.penalty: Penalties of not more than $1,000 if no prior violation within the five-year period, not more than $5,000 if one other violation within the five-year period, and not more than $10,000 if two or more other violations within the seven-year period; director may also order corrective actions and return of the application fee.
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment,

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - written disclosure before accepting application fee
rules.requirement: Before accepting any application fee, a housing provider must disclose in writing whether its eligibility criteria include review of criminal history and that the applicant may provide evidence of inaccuracies, rehabilitation or other mitigating factors.

rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are not covered.
rules.penalty: Penalties of not more than $1,000, $5,000 or $10,000 depending on prior violations.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - prohibited criminal records
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not, before or after a conditional offer, evaluate an applicant based on arrests or charges without conviction, expunged convictions, pardoned convictions, vacated or nullified convictions, juvenile adjudications, or sealed records.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers offering rental dwelling units, other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units are not covered.
rules.penalty: Penalties of not more than $1,000, $5,000 or $10,000 depending on prior violations.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - criminal records that may be considered after conditional offer
rules.requirement: After a conditional offer, a housing provider may consider only convictions for listed serious crimes or lifetime sex offender registration, first-degree offenses within six years, second- or third-degree offenses within four years, and fourth-degree offenses within one year preceding the conditional offer.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - withdrawal of conditional offer
rules.requirement: A housing provider may withdraw a conditional offer based on criminal record only if it determines by preponderance of the evidence that withdrawal is necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest, after an individualized assessment, and must give written notice of the reasons and an opportunity to appeal. On request within 30 days, the provider must provide the information it relied upon free of charge.

rules.effective_date_phrase: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment,

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - discriminatory advertisements
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not publish housing advertisements stating it will not consider applicants who have been arrested or convicted, or otherwise express unlawful limitations as to criminal record, except as the act permits.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers offering rental dwelling units, other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and lifetime sex offender registration requirement.
rules.penalty: Penalties of not more than $1,000, $5,000 or $10,000 depending on prior violations.
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not knowingly or purposefully publish, or cause to be published, any housing advertisement that explicitly provides that the housing provider will not consider any applicant who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses, except for drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment,

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - no drug or alcohol testing of applicants
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not require an applicant to take a drug or alcohol test or request consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers offering rental dwelling units, other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

rules.penalty: Penalties of not more than $1,000, $5,000 or $10,000 depending on prior violations.
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
